item.title: Why are thousands of French students protesting across the country?
item.description: Thousands of French students are protesting over teacher shortages, overcrowded classrooms and poor school conditions, with the movement spreading nationwide ...
item.dc:creator: Vrinda Goel
item.content:encoded: Thousands of students have blocked high schools across France in recent days, protesting against the state of the country’s education system. The movement has triggered violent clashes and riots with police and spread from Paris to other cities, including Montpellier, Nantes and Marseille. More than 5,000 people have been arrested since the protests began, while about 735 educational establishments have been affected, according to the news agency Agence France-Presse (AFP). Meanwhile, up to 500 schools across France will be partially or totally closed on Monday. Lessons will be “totally or partly suspended” in some 400 to 500 high schools as security conditions “have not been fulfilled,” Education Minister Edouard Geffray said. Why are French students protesting? The protests affect lycees, public upper-secondary schools that students usually attend from the ages of 15 to 18, the final three years of secondary education before college. The students’ grievances are numerous, but chief among them are teacher absences, poor classroom conditions, overloaded school timetables and school days that can run from 8 am to 6 pm, which some students say is excessive. The movement began on September 17 at Saint-Exupéry High School in the Paris suburb of Créteil, in support of teachers striking over a lack of staff and resources. It gained momentum and gradually spread across the country over the last week. The situation at Saint-Exupéry High School returned to normal after educational authorities agreed to send additional staff, including a deputy principal and a nurse. How severe have the protests been? French students have set fire to bins and erected blockades outside schools in several cities. Several school principals have been injured, harassed or assaulted during blockades at high schools. Students have also burned barriers on tram tracks. University students have joined the protests, blocking access to about 30 campuses, including in Paris and Marseille, according to a student union. Authorities have reported many dozens of injuries, some from thrown objects and others reportedly from police riot-control projectiles. Students have accused police of using excessive force and causing injuries by regularly firing tear gas canisters to disperse the protests. In Paris on Friday morning, fire damaged the entrances of two high schools. The protests are being further fuelled by the spread of dramatic images and videos on online platforms, notably TikTok. How is the French government responding? On Sunday, French Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu said his government was taking further steps to address the difficulties faced by high school students and educational staff. These included ensuring classes continue, improving facilities, better organising school days and making the French university admissions platform more transparent. Lecornu also said the government was accelerating the review of its “vandal-pays” bill to ensure that those responsible for damage bear the cost of their actions. The government said the students’ grievances were legitimate but condemned what it called “urban violence”. However, the government’s response has failed to satisfy protest organisers, who have called for the demonstrations to continue on Tuesday, accusing the government of a lack of “concrete measures”, according to AFP. The unrest has also taken on a political dimension, becoming entangled in the race to succeed President Emmanuel Macron next May. The government has accused the far-left France Unbowed party of encouraging the protests. Presidential candidate Jean-Luc Melenchon has said that his party had “called for nonviolent methods of struggle” and criticised the government’s response as repressive.

item.title: Former Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon to testify at NYC hearing on AI
item.description: Coxon will appear at request of Council Speaker Julie Menin, who has urged AI whistleblowers to testify as city lawmakers weigh a package of bills aimed at establishing safeguards around technology ...
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg
item.content:encoded: By Nacha Cattan and Laura Nahmias Former Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon, who warned that artificial intelligence could become too powerful for humans to control, will testify Monday at a New York City Council hearing alongside representatives of some of the world’s biggest AI companies.  Coxon will appear at the request of Council Speaker Julie Menin, who has urged AI whistleblowers to testify as city lawmakers weigh a package of bills aimed at establishing safeguards around the technology, according to people familiar with the matter.  Coxon quit Anthropic last month and issued a stark warning about the race to develop increasingly powerful AI, accusing his former employer and OpenAI of “gambling with our lives.” He confirmed he plans to testify on Monday. The hearing will put some of the industry’s most vocal critics in the same room as representatives of Anthropic, OpenAI, Alphabet Inc.’s Google and Meta Platforms Inc.  Former Google DeepMind researcher Alex Turner and Daniel Kokotajlo, executive director of the AI Futures Project and a former OpenAI researcher, are also expected to testify, according to one of the people. The four major AI companies will send policy and safety officials, the person said.  Turner confirmed he plans to attend the hearing. A spokesperson for Google declined to comment. Kokotajlo and representatives of the other companies didn’t respond to requests for comment. The hearing is part of an effort by New York officials to play a larger role in regulating an industry that has expanded rapidly in the city even as much of AI regulation remains the province of federal and state governments. One proposal before the council, sponsored by Menin, would give whistleblowers a portion of fines or penalties recovered from AI companies following reported violations. Other legislation under consideration would allow people harmed by AI systems to sue developers under certain circumstances and require third-party validation of some systems before they can be deployed in the city. OpenAI, Anthropic and Google agreed to appear after Menin’s office warned that they could be subpoenaed, while Meta had committed to attending earlier, Bloomberg News previously reported. The Council subpoenaed SpaceX’s artificial intelligence unit after it failed to respond to requests to appear.

item.title: Trump confuses Brazil with India on prez election, says 125 million voted
item.description: In his Truth Social post, Trump praises the speed of Brazil's vote count but attributes the election to India, which does not directly elect its president ...
item.content:encoded:
Home / World News / Trump confuses Brazil with India on prez election, says 125 million voted

Trump confuses Brazil with India on prez election, says 125 million voted In his Truth Social post, Trump praises the speed of Brazil's vote count but attributes the election to India, which does not directly elect its president

Representative Image: PTI

Unis Ahmad Dar New Delhi 3 min read Last Updated : Oct 05 2026 | 11:17 AM IST

Listen to This Article

Social media users on Monday were puzzled by a post from US President Donald Trump , where he mistook Brazil for India while commenting on the South American country's presidential election.   In a post on Truth Social, Trump claimed that 125 million people had voted in the “first round of India’s Presidential Election,” praising the speed with which results were announced. The election he was referring to, however, was Brazil’s presidential election, held on Sunday.   “125 Million People voted today in the first round of India's Presidential Election ,” Trump wrote, before turning the comparison into another attack on the US electoral system.   Brazil, meanwhile, held the first round of its presidential election on October 4, with incumbent President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and Senator Flávio Bolsonaro emerging as the leading candidates. Neither secured enough votes for an outright victory, setting up a runoff on October 25, according to Reuters.

Brazil's electronic voting system is known for delivering results rapidly, which was apparently the feature Trump wanted to highlight while making his case against the US voting system. More than 159 million Brazilians were eligible to vote in Sunday's election. Also Read

Delhi to remain hot today; heavy rain likely in parts of South India

Flavio Bolsonaro pushes Lula to brink of defeat ahead of Brazil runoff

Attempting to compare the US electoral system with the Brazilian election, Trump claimed that vote counts in Detroit, Philadelphia, California and other US cities and states can take weeks to be “calculated”, before declaring: “Voting in America is CORRUPT!!!”   Although he did not name Brazil, the timing of the post and his reference to roughly 125 million voters closely match Sunday’s Brazilian presidential election, suggesting that the Brazilian vote was the example he intended to cite.

Trump’s post invited reactions from social media with one user commenting, “Trump living in a different world? Is a presidential election taking place in India? President Donald Trump made the incorrect claim that 125 million people voted in India's "presidential election" today.”   Another said, “This man is the president of the most powerful country in the world. This didn't happen by accident; he's done this before.” One more comment read: “Trump is suffering from India syndrome.”   India does not hold a direct presidential election   India does not hold a direct presidential election. The Indian president is elected by an electoral college comprising elected members of Parliament and state legislatures, rather than through a nationwide popular vote. The next presidential election is not due in 2026.

item.title: HDFC Bank: Anup Bagchi at helm lifts overhang; brokerages share outlook
item.description: Analysts at Motilal Oswal Financial Services (MOFSL) said Bagchi's appointment removes a key overhang around HDFC Bank's leadership succession.
item.content:encoded:
Home / Markets / News / HDFC Bank: Anup Bagchi at helm lifts overhang; brokerages share outlook

HDFC Bank: Anup Bagchi at helm lifts overhang; brokerages share outlook Analysts at Motilal Oswal Financial Services (MOFSL) said Bagchi's appointment removes a key overhang around HDFC Bank's leadership succession.

MOFSL expects the bank’s operating performance to improve from FY28E onward, supported by a recovery in loan growth and margins.Image Credit: Bloomberg

Saloni Goel New Delhi 4 min read Last Updated : Oct 05 2026 | 9:12 AM IST

Listen to This Article

HDFC Bank share price : The Reserve Bank of India's (RBI) nod to Anup Bagchi as the next managing director (MD) and chief executive officer (CEO) for India's largest private lender, HDFC Bank, clears a major leadership overhang and is being seen as a long-term positive for its stock.    Bagchi, appointed for a three-year term, would succeed Sashidhar Jagdishan, whose tenure ends on October 26, 2026. An ICICI Bank veteran and current MD & CEO of ICICI Life, Bagchi brings in over three decades of experience across banking, capital markets, wealth management and insurance. READ MORE   Analysts at Motilal Oswal Financial Services (MOFSL) said the appointment of Bagchi removes a key overhang surrounding HDFC Bank's leadership succession and brings an external perspective at a time when the bank is seeking to rebuild investor confidence.

Also Read

Not just poor price performance, HDFC Bank has been marred by corporate governance issues lately, among other issues. The stock has declined 27 per cent so far this year and eroded investor wealth worth ₹4.12 trillion during this period, ACE Equity data shows.   Also Read | HDFC Bank shares rise 2% as Street cheers Anup Bagchi's appointment as CEO   Management change to aid investor sentiment Emkay Global said that Bagchi should help restore investor and customer confidence in the bank, given that he is a banking veteran with experience across diverse responsibilities within the ICICI Bank group.

Moreover, an external appointment could provide  HDFC Bank  with a cleaner slate to reassess its strategy, challenge existing practices and drive a strategic reset. Nomura analysts believe that the pace of execution and clarity on the medium-term growth strategy will be critical for investor confidence and a sustained re-rating. It has a 'Buy' rating and target price of ₹950 on the shares of HDFC Bank, valuing the core bank at 1.9x Mar-28F BVPS of ₹446, with subsidiaries contributing ₹105/share.   Nuvama Institutional Research said it views the development as a long-term positive; however, blending the distinct ICICI and HDFC Bank organisational DNA could pose near-term challenges with potential management rejig across businesses/subsidiaries. Therefore, rebuilding the leadership team, sustaining growth, bolstering governance and restoring stakeholder confidence would be key priorities, it said.

Focus areas & impact on earnings Commenting on the key focus areas, Emkay said over the coming quarters, it sees key priorities for the new MD as: ensuring stability in the upper management; reviving deposit growth; improving the productivity of newer branches; upscaling technological and digital capabilities to match leading peers; and strengthening processes to move beyond past issues, including instances of mis-selling.    Overall, MOFSL expects the bank’s operating performance to improve from FY28E onward, supported by a recovery in loan growth and margins. It currently estimates earnings to grow in the mid-teens in FY28E after sluggish trends over FY24-27E. It retained 'Buy' with a target price of ₹925 (1.8x FY28E ABV + ₹128 for subs).

Scope to re-rate Analysts further see re-rating scope for HDFC Bank amid timely execution on key areas of growth. Analysts at Jefferies said that timely changes to the team (if any) and opportunities from (1) improving retail detail growth, (2) better cross-sell fees, and (3) calibrated re-risking of loan-mix will aid earnings and re-rating from an attractive 1.4x FY28E adj PB.    The prolonged underperformance of HDFC Bank shares has also made the valuation attractive, and the stock should see a "sustained re-rating" as the new leadership delivers on key priorities and geopolitical uncertainty-led FPI outflows moderate or reverse, said Emkay Global.   Disclaimer: Views and outlook shared belong to the respective brokerages/analysts and are not endorsed by Business Standard. Readers' discretion is advised.
